references.text: The continuation of the law concerning fights between men, describing the compensation the guilty party must pay when the injured person recovers.
Also deals with physical conflict between men and the consequences of violence during a quarrel.
Describes the use of stones as weapons in violent conflicts, distinguishing between murder and other injuries.
Abner's fight with Asahel illustrates a situation where men are fighting and one is killed, related to conflicts between men.
Describes a sick man lying in bed, similar to the expression 'laid up' in the Exodus text.
Jesus expands on the law concerning murder and anger, referring to the Old Testament command not to kill, which includes violence leading to injury.
Both verses specify how the legislation handles damage caused by stones, and together they elaborate on the principle of liability based on intent and circumstances.
The verses form a thematic parallel in the penal code of the books of Moses, where together they outline the criteria for distinguishing between intentional violence and accidental harm.
